prompt: An evening theater ticket counter painted in opaque gouache on textured paper. A small tangerine-orange paper ticket rests on top of white cotton gloves on the counter. Compose close enough to see soft stitched seams, matte white highlights, and the indigo-violet evening light in their folds. The saturated orange ticket and its crisp little silhouette catch the eye first. Keep the surrounding booth quiet and subdued. Visible opaque strokes, no digital glow.

A woodblock print of a wave surging over a breakwater, pulled in one single navy-blue ink on off-white paper. Reserve the unprinted paper for the froth breaking over the top and curling down the wall. Long fine horizontal cuts describe the distant sea; hefty dark angular shapes and a few glistening carved streaks describe the wet stones in the foreground. Hand-cut irregularities in the edges, ink on the raised wood and bare paper, no additional ink colors.

One horizontal charcoal drawing in two equal side-by-side panels, the same neighborhood bicycle repair shop reopening after closure. Repeat the distinctive arched workshop doorway, worn workbench and pegboard in the two panels. Left: the mechanic has rolled the shutter up and is actively fixing a customer's bicycle, wrench at the axle. Right: nobody anywhere; the open threshold, freshly swept track in old dust, one freshly repaired bicycle ready to collect and tools recently used on the bench tell the story through human traces. Independent views, one consistent shop. Expressive charcoal marks and rubbed shadows on paper. No letters, lettering, words, numerals or signs anywhere.

One two-panel black ink comic, with a thin gutter. Exactly one person in each panel: the same short-haired adult wearing a plain cuffed jacket and dark shoes sitting alone on the same rooftop bench. Consistent bench slats, parapet, skyline and soft overcast late-afternoon light. Left: from across a stretch of empty rooftop, they hunch at the end of the bench, shoulders drawn in, gaze lowered, ink shadows cutting off the space, a feeling of exclusion. Right: shift closer to their profile; still alone on the bench, shoulders released, leaning back comfortably, gazing at the same skyline in quiet chosen solitude. Loose confident brush-ink contours and spare hatching. No dialogue, captions, lettering or thought balloons.

An on-the-spot street sketch of a shopper's paper grocery bag at the instant its bottom has torn open. Frame the hand, both paper handles, the split bottom and pavement together. The hand is still gripping the attached handles. Show ragged paper flaps bent apart, a few round mandarins suspended below the opening at different heights in their fall, and a single mandarin that has already reached the sidewalk with its small contact shadow. Gestural pen and light washes on sketchbook paper, subdued street details, orange fruit easy to see.

An unretouched documentary photograph taken from the side of a single straight row of dominoes on a wooden desk at the instant a chain reaction travels from frame left to frame right. Camera at desk level, looking across the row; keep the whole run in focus. At the left the spent tiles overlap nearly flat, tops pointing right. Toward midframe the rightward lean progressively decreases, and the leading falling tile's upper edge is just touching the left side of the very next tile. On the right the remaining dominoes stand vertical at regular spacing. One continuous row on the same baseline; freeze motion with a short exposure. Soft natural light, no illustrative arrows, no additional rows.

Quiet realistic interior photograph of an old library. Exactly one book hangs motionless and unsupported in open air above an unobstructed patch of worn wooden floor. One loose leaf from that book has already fallen flat and completely at rest directly beneath it on the floorboards. Frame both objects clearly at a three-quarter angle, with some air around the suspended volume. A nearby ordinary chair rests on its feet and the other books are shelved normally. Soft window light, understated color, natural shadows, old paper and wood grain. No other floating objects or magical effects.

A field watercolor painted on location at a small fishing-village harbor just after the tide has gone out. A modest weathered fishing boat has settled onto exposed, still-wet tidal mud, its hull visibly bearing on the soft ground. Behind it a narrow channel still holds water. Along the quay and mooring piles the dark wet band and tideline mark show where the water stood; little rivulets run through reflective mud toward the channel. Transparent washes, economical strokes and pencil construction on cold-pressed paper. Give the grounded boat and remaining channel an uncluttered, legible relationship.
